## Passage 1: The Environmental Cost of Industrial Prosperity

The ==aftermath== of the industrial revolution, which began long ==ago== in the northern ==province== of the country, continues to cast a long shadow over the modern world. In the decades ==after== the first factories appeared, the region ==prosper==ed enormously, its ==prosperity== built upon the relentless extraction of ==crude== oil, ==iron== ore, and ==aluminium== — or, as the British spell it, ==aluminum==. The cities grew wealthy, and their citizens grew ==proud== of their ==prosperous== towns. Yet beneath the gleaming surface of progress lay a profound environmental crisis. Rivers that once ran ==crystal== clear were now choked with industrial waste; factories would routinely ==dump== toxic chemicals into waterways that farmers depended on to ==irrigate== their fields. The ==air==, once fresh and invigorating, hung heavy with the ==fume==s of burning ==rubber== and smelting metals.

The damage to the atmosphere was ==also== severe. Scientists had ==already== warned that the thinning of the ==ozone== layer above the region was accelerating, a consequence of decades of unchecked industrial emissions. ==Albeit== the warnings had been issued repeatedly, industrialists continued to expand their operations. One particular ==agent==, representing a coalition of chemical manufacturers, would ==administer== a public relations campaign designed to ==rub==bish the scientific evidence. He was not ==afraid== to use ==rude== language when dismissing environmentalists, calling their concerns "==dumb== hysteria." His arrogance was staggering — he seemed to believe that the ==surroundings== could absorb any amount of punishment, that nature itself would silently ==surrender== to human ambition.

It was in this climate of denial that a young environmental scientist named Dr. Elena Voss began her research. She had ==accustom==ed herself to the hostility of the industrial lobby, having grown up in a farming community where every ==acre== of land mattered. Her father had been an ==actor== in the local theatre before turning to ==agriculture==, and her mother, a former ==actress==, had taught her to speak ==aloud== with conviction. Dr. Voss discovered that the ==crust== of the earth in the mining regions had been so severely destabilised that entire hillsides were at risk of collapse. The ==protein== content of local crops had diminished significantly, and the ==animal== population — from the smallest ==ant== to the largest mammal — was in sharp decline. She published her findings in a prestigious scientific ==album== — a peer-reviewed journal — and the data provoked widespread ==protest== from both the public and the scientific community.

The government, under mounting pressure, was forced to act. A new legislative ==provision== was introduced, mandating stricter environmental regulations for all industrial operations. The law aimed to ==protect== the remaining natural habitats and to ==prosecute== companies that violated the new standards. ==Further==more, it established a framework for restoring damaged ecosystems, requiring polluters to ==furnish== financial compensation to affected communities. The ==futile== resistance of the industrial lobby only served to ==irritate== the public further, and their attempts to ==bypass== the regulations through legal loopholes were ultimately unsuccessful. The ==fuss== they created in the media was short-lived; the evidence was simply too compelling to ignore.

### 中文翻译：工业繁荣的环境代价

工业革命始于该国北部省份很久以前，其后果至今仍在现代世界投下长长的阴影。在第一批工厂出现之后的几十年里，该地区经济蓬勃发展，其繁荣建立在无情开采原油、铁矿石和铝的基础上。城市变得富裕，市民们为他们繁华的城镇感到自豪。然而，在进步的光鲜表面之下隐藏着深刻的生态危机。曾经清澈见底的河流现在被工业废物堵塞；工厂常常将有毒化学品倾倒入农民赖以灌溉田地的水道中。空气曾经清新而令人振奋，现在却因燃烧橡胶和冶炼金属的废气而变得沉重。

对大气层的损害也同样严重。科学家们已经警告说，该地区上空臭氧层的稀薄正在加速，这是数十年不受控制的工业排放的后果。尽管警告已经反复发出，工业家们仍继续扩大他们的业务。一位代表化学制造商联盟的代理人发起了一场公关运动，旨在诋毁科学证据。他在驳斥环保主义者时并不害怕使用粗鲁的语言，称他们的担忧为"愚蠢的歇斯底里"。他的傲慢令人震惊——他似乎认为周围环境可以吸收任何程度的破坏，自然本身会默默地向人类野心投降。

正是在这种否认的氛围中，一位名叫埃琳娜·沃斯博士的年轻环境科学家开始了她的研究。她已经习惯了工业游说团体的敌意，她在一个每英亩土地都至关重要的农业社区长大。她的父亲曾在当地剧院当过演员，后来转向了农业，而她的母亲，一位前女演员，教会了她大声而有信念地说话。沃斯博士发现，采矿区的地壳已经被严重破坏，整个山坡都有坍塌的危险。当地农作物的蛋白质含量显著下降，动物种群——从最小的蚂蚁到最大的哺乳动物——都在急剧减少。她将研究结果发表在了一本享有盛誉的科学专辑——一本同行评审的期刊上——这些数据引发了公众和科学界的广泛抗议。

在日益增长的压力下，政府被迫采取行动。一项新的立法条款被引入，要求对所有工业作业实施更严格的环境法规。该法律旨在保护剩余的自然栖息地，并起诉违反新标准的公司。此外，它还建立了一个恢复受损生态系统的框架，要求污染者向受影响的社区提供经济赔偿。工业游说团体徒劳的抵抗只是进一步激怒了公众，他们试图通过法律漏洞绕过法规的努力最终失败了。他们在媒体上制造的大惊小怪是短暂的；证据实在太令人信服，不容忽视。

## Passage 2: An Archaeological Revelation — The Lost Dynasty

In the remote ==isle== off the eastern coast, a team of researchers made a discovery that would reshape our understanding of ancient civilisations. The ==archaeology== — or, as the Americans prefer, ==archaeology== — expedition had been underway for nearly a decade when, on a sweltering ==afternoon==, a graduate student uncovered a fragment of ==ivory== buried beneath the ==crust== of a collapsed temple. The find was extraordinary: the fragment bore inscriptions that pointed to a previously unknown ==dynasty==, one that had ==prosper==ed in isolation for centuries. The team, led by the renowned ==archaeology== professor Dr. James Whitmore, worked tirelessly to excavate the site, carefully brushing away centuries of dust with the precision of a ==musician== tuning a ==musical== instrument.

The artefacts they uncovered were breathtaking. A ceremonial ==prototype== of a royal sceptre, carved from a single piece of ==crystal==, suggested a level of craftsmanship that rivalled any known civilisation of the era. The ==royalty== of this lost kingdom had clearly lived in opulence: gold ornaments, intricately woven ==fur== garments, and an extensive ==album== of painted scrolls depicting scenes of courtly life. The ==ownership== of these lands, the scrolls revealed, had been a source of constant conflict. One particularly ==cruel== king had ==provoke==d a rebellion by seizing the ==owner==ship of farmlands from peasants who ==owe==d him tribute — lands they had cultivated for generations and now ==owing== enormous debts they could never repay.

Dr. Whitmore noted that the kingdom's decline was as dramatic as its rise. As rival factions fought for control, the once-==prosperous== cities fell into ==ruin==. The final king, faced with an invading army, chose to ==surrender== rather than see his people ==crush==ed beneath the wheels of war. He was not a ==mute== figurehead — historical records suggest he ==mutter==ed a famous soliloquy before laying down his arms — but his decision to yield was nonetheless seen as an act of profound dignity. The kingdom's legacy, ==irrespective== of its violent end, endured in the cultural memory of the region. The ==royal== archives, preserved in the dry desert air, contained detailed records of agricultural practices, including innovative methods to ==irrigate== arid land and cultivate ==protein==-rich crops.

The discovery has ==further== implications for our understanding of ancient trade networks. Traces of ==supersonic== — well, perhaps not supersonic, but remarkably swift — maritime trade routes connected this ==isle== to distant civilisations. Ships carrying ==ivory==, ==crystal==, and dyed textiles — coloured with a rare purple ==dye== extracted from local sea snails — sailed across open waters in a remarkable ==cruise== of commerce and cultural exchange. The ==dynasty== had not been as ==isolate==d as scholars once believed; it was connected to a wider world, engaging in trade that would make any modern ==supermarket== seem provincial by comparison.

### 中文翻译：考古发现——失落的王朝

在东海岸外的偏远岛屿上，一组研究人员取得了一项将重塑我们对古代文明理解的发现。考古学——或者如美国人偏好的拼法，考古学——探险已经进行了近十年，在一个酷热的下午，一名研究生在倒塌神庙的地壳下发现了一枚象牙碎片。这一发现非同寻常：碎片上刻有铭文，指向一个先前未知的王朝，该王朝在孤立中繁荣了数个世纪。由著名的考古学教授詹姆斯·惠特莫尔博士领导的团队不知疲倦地挖掘这个遗址，以音乐家调试乐器的精确度仔细刷去几个世纪的尘土。

他们发现的文物令人叹为观止。一根由整块水晶雕刻而成的皇家权杖原型，暗示着与那个时代任何已知文明相媲美的工艺水平。这个失落王国的王室显然生活奢华：金饰、精编织的毛皮服装，以及一本描绘宫廷生活场景的大量画卷专辑。卷轴揭示，这些土地的所有权一直是持续冲突的根源。一位特别残忍的国王通过从欠他贡赋的农民手中夺取耕地所有权而引发了一场叛乱——这些土地是农民世代耕种的，而现在他们因欠下永远无法偿还的巨额债务而苦苦挣扎。

惠特莫尔博士指出，该王国的衰落与其崛起一样戏剧化。随着敌对派系争夺控制权，曾经繁华的城市沦为废墟。末代国王面对入侵军队，选择投降而不是让他的人民在战车轮下被碾碎。他不是一个沉默的傀儡——历史记录表明他在放下武器之前喃喃自语了一段著名的独白——但他屈服的决定仍被视为一种深刻的尊严之举。这个王国的遗产，无论其暴力的终结如何，在该地区的文化记忆中延续下来。保存在干燥沙漠空气中的皇家档案包含了农业实践的详细记录，包括灌溉干旱土地和种植富含蛋白质作物的创新方法。

这一发现对我们理解古代贸易网络有着更深远的含义。超音速——嗯，也许不是超音速，但确实非常迅速的——海上贸易路线将这个岛屿与遥远的文明连接起来。载着象牙、水晶和染色纺织品——用从当地海螺中提取的稀有紫色染料染色——的船只在开阔水域航行，进行着商业和文化交流的非凡巡航。这个王朝并不像学者们曾经认为的那样孤立；它连接着更广阔的世界，参与的贸易使任何现代超市相比之下都显得狭隘。

抗议活动开始时相当和平。一位知名女演员，她一直直言不讳地倡导人权，以一种具有音乐品质的声音向人群讲话，引人注目。她谈到一个声称捍卫自由却系统性地破坏自由的政府的讽刺。她的话语特别有分量，因为她自己的兄弟，一名前情报代理人，正是根据同一法律因揭露政府腐败而被起诉。他被剥夺了对一家小型独立报纸的所有权，目前正在服长期监禁。另一家出版物的所有者也成为了目标，他选择交出他的出版许可证而不是面临起诉——这个决定虽然短期内看来是徒劳的，但成为了抵抗的有力象征。

    69→### 中文翻译：正义、抗议与一个国家的改革
